notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23, head d04061d, skill_hash 005deae0...): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0, a model_id matching the requested model and reads of SKILL.md and library-design.md; each transcript shows Read calls on both files before the Write of weather.ex.

git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes two rules in the case's list, "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" (three new paragraphs) and "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" (rewritten), and adds one sentence to the ex_unit.md logging rule, which no run exercises. The other nine rules are unchanged and graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/library-client-skill.json; the two changed rules are graded against their current text, as in evals/sweeps/2026-10-23-check/grades/library-client-skill.json.

Read required keys: the sentence that decides the verdict is "A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long." The rule names maps and structs, so opts[:key] on the keyword list Keyword.validate!/2 returns (opus-1 line 150, haiku-2 line 46, sonnet-1 line 109, sonnet-2 line 103) is outside it. Case bullet 1 (a body does not re-match one atom key or struct field out of a held value): 0 of 5 runs violated; 5 of 5 exercised it, each reading client or response fields with dot access in a body.

In multi-clause functions: the sentence that decides the verdict is "A field no pattern or guard in the clause uses, bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines, makes the reader scan every head to find what selects." Case bullet 2 (no body-only field bound in every head of a three-plus-clause function, nor in a spread head): 0 of 5 runs violated, reading "bound in every clause" as the same field in every clause, as the check batch did. 4 of 5 exercised the three-plus-clause shape (opus-1 Error.message/1 and handle_response/1, haiku-1 handle_response/1, sonnet-1 Error.message/1 and handle_response/1, sonnet-2 Error.message/1 and parse_response/1); haiku-2 has only two-clause functions. Spread heads: sonnet-1 (lines 175-179) and sonnet-2 (lines 156-160) spread and bind only keys their guards read, which the rule allows; haiku-1's line 159 would spread under mix format and also binds only guard-read keys. Under the other reading (every head binds some body-only field, not the same one), 2 of 5 would be violated: sonnet-1 Error.message/1 (lines 25, 29, 33, 37 bind status; status and detail; detail; exception) and sonnet-2 parse_response/1 (lines 143, 147, 152 bind body; message; status and body). opus-1's Error.message/1 takes the struct whole with = error in all four heads, the form the rule's example shows. The rule and bullet still leave this reading open; I would say in the rule that the field is the same field in every clause, since that is what the example shows and what decides these two runs.

Make polymorphism explicit, unchanged rule, decided by "an `api_key` taken from `opts` and put straight into a request header is unchecked input": haiku-2 violates it (line 45 into line 80, confirmed with a stub Req: new(api_key: ~c"k") returns a client). The other four check the key: opus-1 and haiku-1 in a guarded validator, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 as a guarded positional argument of new/2, which the d sweep counted as clean for its sonnet-2.

opus-1's @doc false Forecast.parse/1 returns a bare :error (line 27), which handle_response/1 wraps in %Error{reason: :invalid_response} (line 205) before any caller sees it; graded clean for Use exception structs and Return, as the 2026-10-22-b grade did for its sonnet-2's from_body/1. The check batch flagged haiku-1's {:error, :invalid_body}, an atom reason inside an error tuple; a bare :error carries no reason for the rule to govern.

Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as in the d sweep: Match every expected shape is flagged where an error doc names a status class the catch-all clause does not keep to. sonnet-1 documents :api_error as a 4xx or 5xx status (line 7) and sends 302 there (line 171); haiku-1 documents :invalid_response as a success status with a bad body (line 11) and sends 302, and a 201 carrying a valid forecast, there (line 151); both confirmed with a stub Req. opus-1 documents its catch-all as any status other than 200, sonnet-2 documents :invalid_response as a status or body the API does not document, and haiku-2 defines no reason kinds, so none is flagged. The private get_forecast/3 in haiku-1 and haiku-2 names an HTTP request, not a key lookup, and is not counted under Naming, as in the 2026-10-22 grades. haiku-1's private validate!/1 raises ArgumentError for invalid options, which library-design.md allows, as in earlier sweeps.

Before you finish is flagged only where the file fails mix format --check-formatted: haiku-1 fails at line 159 (it checked syntax with Code.string_to_quoted!/1 and ran no formatter); the other four pass (rechecked in the scratch folder). opus-1 ran mix format --check-formatted and compiled against a stub Req; sonnet-1 ran mix format and compiled; sonnet-2's format check was blocked; haiku-2 ran no shell command.

Not graded, as in the previous sweeps, but noted in the summaries and matching result.json compiles: opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile apart from the absent Req; haiku-2 does not, because WeatherClient (line 91) and Forecast (line 136) build %WeatherClient.Error{} before the file defines it (line 139). With the modules reordered in the scratch folder and a stub Req, a charlist key raises ArgumentError in opus-1 and haiku-1 and FunctionClauseError in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, and is accepted by haiku-2.
